catalog_quote: 4. SUPRASEGMENTALS. Stress in Irarutu language is phonemic. The stress is identified by high pitch when the stressed syllable is not followed by the syllable with a schwa. Vowel length does not occur on the stressed syllable. /debé/ [dəbé] 'pukul' 'to hit'; /tepú/ [təpú] 'di bawah' 'under'; /pití/ ... 'a kind of mouse'; /waráda/ [wařáda] 'pisau' 'knife'; /wararú/ [wařařú] 'berita' 'news'. [p.48] The vowel length occurs in the stressed syllable when the stressed syllable is followed by the syllable with a schwa. In such cases, a gliding pitch also occurs on the stressed syllable. /dábe/ [dá:bə] 'menumbuk, memukul' 'to pound'; /tápe/ [tá:pə] 'menikam' 'to stab'; /píte/ [pí:tə] 'jahat' 'evil'; /rádeni/ [řá:dənɩ] 'pakaian' 'clothing'; /dedáne/ [dədá:nə] 'kebun' 'garden'. ... audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding passage is verbatim on printed p.47 (PDF p.18) of the held Matsumura 1991 PDF, page image inspected; p.48 and endnote 2 p.55 match the scanned layer. (2) Deciding source is a 1991 SIL/UNCEN phonology working paper; the best available description, Jackson 2014 (451-pp reference grammar with a dedicated 'Stress and accent' section and a spectrogram), is already on file under morphstress_f2 and independently states 'Stress in Irarutu is not predictable... lexically determined... Irarutu has phonemic stress', with final and penultimate stress about equally frequent and minimal pair [fi.'na] vs ['fi.na]. So LEXICAL is confirmed by the strongest source; nothing suggests a recode. (3) Voorhoeve 1989 fetched sources now (IRIAN 17, Wayback of papuaweb): 'Stress is phonemic... however the stress usually is on the last vowel phoneme' — this is the primary basis of StressTyp2 U

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, Clemens L. (1989). Notes on Irarutu (an Austronesian language spoken in the centre of the Bomberai Peninsula, Southwest Irian Jaya). IRIAN: Bulletin of Irian Jaya 17: 107-119.
sources.quote: p.110: 'Stress is phonemic as shown by: ɔrɔ'e nggáta "who are you?" - ərə' nga tá "you eat shit". In words with more than one vowel phoneme however the stress usually is on the last vowel phoneme: e.g. fan "pig".' p.111: 'In polysyllabic words stress will be marked when it is carried by another vowel than the last one.' Also p.110: the non-phonemic final [ə] 'can serve as the carrier of stress when a word is uttered in isolation and with extra emphasis'.
